results.summary_before: Despite its title and one-line description referring to a Jabulani ball VGA demo, the documentation describes a PRBS31 generator built from a 31-bit Fibonacci LFSR with feedback from registers 30 and 27, whose output is taken off-chip and fed back for analysis. The pin list matches the Tiny VGA pinout, and the design is clocked at 25.175 MHz, but the described PRBS behavior does not match the VGA pin functions. A silicon test report from a tester states that it is a bouncing ball demo that appears to work as intended while the documentation seems unrelated. The mismatch between the documentation and the observed silicon behavior makes the design's actual function unclear.

results.summary_before: This project implements a minimal 8-bit CPU with a simple datapath and two finite-state machines. It accepts serial input data through the ui_in pins and provides an 8-bit output along with carry, zero, overflow, and negative flags. A start signal triggers serial input, and multiplexer select lines control internal routing. No external hardware is required for operation.

results.summary_before: TinyTapeStation is a retro gaming console that plays a single pre-loaded game called Gnome Knight, controlled with an NES or SNES gamepad. It outputs 640x480 VGA video and analog audio, and supports standard retro controller layouts with simple remapping. The design requires a gamepad PMOD or direct NES controller wiring, a VGA monitor, and speakers or an amplifier. A silicon test report notes that the game starts up and characters move, though the tester did not have a SNES controller.

results.summary_before: This is a simple 8-bit CPU inspired by Ben Eater's design and the game Turing Complete, created in a four-hour sprint before the submission deadline. It has an 8-bit input bus and an 8-bit output bus, with no bidirectional pins used. Testing requires an RP2040 or RP2350 on a test board acting as a memory controller to run programs. The documentation is sparse and does not detail the instruction set or architecture.

A 7-segment display is listed as external hardware, though its role is unclear. The project is a simple test of basic logic gates.
